direction.comments: The direction on a macroscale feels pretty standard in relation to how surrealist/meta the actual movie is, but it does change its style in relation to how Kaufman changed the narrative tone of the script; The microscale is good because it is really Nic Cage talking with himself the entire time, painting this inner monologue of doubt and social anxiety; Storytelling is so meta that it is incredibly funny because, at the surface, it is a movie about Charlie Kaufman being optioned to write an adaptation for this story, which is in turn adapting Meryl Streep’s character writing an adaptation of her short story, which in turn is an adaptation of her experience with the subject; The movie's storytelling also shifts from being this smug, fake-deep movie to a climax that is very dramatic and action-packed after Kaufman meets McKee and the latter tells him he needs to add drama to the story, putting the cherry on top of what is already an incredibly meta story; Tension is only really added in the end when they artificially create this action and drama to make the story have some substance for the audience, adding to the meta-commentary on the source material’s adaptation process

performance.comments: Role really feels written for him as he is able to use his quirky charm and ability to play off himself in this dual role well to help show the social anxiety and self-doubt Charlie Kaufman has, especially when juxtaposed with his more confident, yet less intelligent fake, twin brother; has good chemistry with himself in this dual role as he is intentionally awkward with the rest of the cast
Gives a very Meryl Streep performance; she showed up, did her job, and got rewarded for it
Plays his role well as he helps capture the free-spirited side of America that makes for a great subject in a story; has good chemistry with Meryl Streep
Literally gives a glimpse into what would eventually become his role in 'Succession' as Logan Roy

cast.comments: Everyone plays their role well in helping Charlie Kaufman feel like a social outcast as they try to connect with him, but he phsyically cannot due to his social anxiety and self-doubt

story.comments: The concept is the most Charlie Kaufman meta concept ever because this movie is a semi-autobiographical take on Kaufman's own struggles with adapting "The Orchid Thief" to film, so he basically inserts himself into the story and makes the movie about this struggle, which then meta-textually looks into Streep's character's own struggles with adapting the story from her short story, which then meta-textually looks into her own struggles adapting the short story from her own life experiences with John Laroche; The plot structure is so meta that I love it because the movie is basically this meta-pyramid of Kaufman trying to get into Susan Orlean's head as he tries to adapt her book, but is so meta in its commentary that after he meets Robert McKee, who tells him to add drama and stakes to his story, the movie literally shifts into this dramatic, action-packed climax that is completely different from the first half and is also just made up and did not happen in real life; Character writing is very good as the movie examines Kaufman's own struggles with social anxiety and self-doubt and uses this fake twin to basically amplify how he is feeling while adapting this story

screenplay.comments: The dialogue is very Charlie Kaufman with its meta-commentary, wit, quirkiness, and surrealism; The humor is good and helps make this feel like a Charlie Kaufman-Spike Jonze comedy; The symbolism is very strong as the whole movie is a commentary on the struggles of the adaptation process and provides a very accurate depiction of social anxiety and self-doubt; The foreshadowing is funny because the shift at the end makes this movie feel more Hollywood, but is also so funny because it obviously did not happen in real life; The movie does close off well and helps show Kaufman's growth as a character

score.comments: Used minimally, but does establish tone when used

editing.comments: Very standard editing, especially from the time period

production_design.comments: It was fun to see them use the "Being John Malkovich" sets in this movie to help amplify the film's meta-commentary

makeup.comments: Even though Charlie Kaufman's sweat makeup is intentionally bad to amplify how anxious he is, it still is pretty obvious and looks fake; His balding hair is also pretty obvious

review.pacing: Pacing is right for the most part and picks up in the climax when the tone shifts
review.climax: The climax is very funny considering how the movie shifts from being this meta-commentary on adaptation to being this Hollywood action movie just because Robert McKee told Charlie Kaufman he needed to add drama and stakes, especially when you consider none of this actually happened
review.tone: Tone is very much a meta-comedy that feels very similar in style to Spike Jonze and Charlie Kaufman's other works; The tonal shift at the end helps amplify the meta-commentary about the adaptation process
review.overall: Overall, "Adaptation" is a good meta-comedy that is very Charlie Kaufman in that the movie highlights his own struggles with adapting "The Orchid Thief" into a film, so instead of adapting the story, he wrote about himself adapting the story, looking at the different layers of the adaptation process in a meta way; the movie works because Nic Cage is the perfect actor to capture both Charlie Kaufman and his fake twin brother, and Kaufman is able to use this meta-commentary to show his own frustrations with not only the adaptation process but his own social anxiety after finding newfound fame after writing "Being John Malkovich"
